abilities.name: Cultivate plants
abilities.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; tend plots; abandon unfinished planting.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1 energy: dig, then place and cover the unit; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Tend: target a planted plot in reach; one round, 0.5 energy. Abandon: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
abilities.effects: Digging keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It establishes only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 20 rounds, optional checks at 5, 10 and 20; not a growth date. Tend checks the plot and its 0.6 m clearance, kept free of plants by the plant rules; it removes nothing and adds no water, nutrient or growth. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Abandon, or death, before placement returns the unit once (where the person died); a placed unit stays. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Two paid one-round stages; job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stage after revalidation; completion, failure, abandoning and death settle once. Growth runs only in ordinary simulation.

abilities.name: Heat-prepare food
abilities.function: Heat-prepare owned food on an open hearth: clear a bed, light it by hand-drill friction, feed fuel, roast and turn food, inspect, retrieve, smother or cancel.
abilities.costs: Study 3 rounds. Unless stated, a mode takes 1 round. prepare-hearth: x,y in reach on dry open ground 0.7 m clear of objects, loose items and people; 2 paid rounds of 1 energy clear a 0.45 m bed, no stock. tend: inputs owned branch, bark or dry-grass in tenths (bed holds 8 mass) and/or turn:true; 0.5 energy. ignite: unlit hearth loaded with dry-grass 0.5 and branch 0.5; board one owned branch or willow, spindle one owned harder birch or oak; up to 12 drilling rounds of 1.5 energy, then ember transfer and first tending at 0.5 each; repeat ignite to continue. cook: inputs one whole owned root or berry (quantity 1); 0.5 energy. inspect: target, or up to 4 inputs; 0.2 energy. retrieve or extinguish: 0.5 energy. cancel: no energy. Gather and travel cost extra.
abilities.effects: Fuel and wood moisture starts at current rain, +0.08*rain per rainy round, else -0.01*(1+wind). Drilling wears a socket and makes dust; an ember forms only when 2 g of dust reaches 350 C (20 W drill; wind cools, moisture cuts, none above 0.35; warms with consecutive rounds), else the trial fails after 12 rounds, leaving worn pieces and dust. Drilling and transfer need rain<=0.15, wind<=0.65, fuel moisture<=0.35; an unworked ember dies. A lit fire burns at most 1 fuel unit per round times dryness (10% ash), keeps embers 3 rounds, is doused by rain>0.6 and catches loose fuel on its rim. Heat: 2 MJ per fuel unit, 18 minutes per round (heat only); the bed stores and loses heat; food on it heats from below, loses water at 100 C and chars above 200 C once dry. Cooked: core 85 C for 10 minutes; charred: 20% of solids burnt. Handling on a bed over 60 C or food over 50 C needs an owned branch as a stick; raked-aside food cools. Retrieved food keeps its age and spoilage and eats as one unit at its original nutrition times its unburnt solids share; char stays as residue. No detoxification, preservation, warmth or reward. Inspect records perceivable state and a model estimate, not core temperature.

execution.progress: Paid clearing and drilling rounds; job and reserved pieces persist; an unworked round pauses unpaid; resuming rechecks reach, pieces, fuel and weather. Fire, bed and food change only in actual rounds, also after cancel or death.

abilities.name: Examine and open food
abilities.function: Examine an owned food unit for perceivable condition and your own records about it, or open its outer layer by hand or by striking it with an owned implement on a solid support; cancel unfinished opening.
abilities.costs: Study 1 round. Each mode takes 1 round. examine: inputStackId, an owned food stack; 0.2 energy; nothing is used. open: inputStackId, one whole owned untreated food unit (quantity 1); 0.5 energy per performed round. Bare hands open only soft food. A strike needs toolIds with one owned whole inedible rigid implement and supportTargetId, a solid object in reach. Missing or unsuitable prerequisites, or energy below 0.5, are reported as blocked and cost nothing. open again resumes paused work after rechecking unit, implement, support, reach and energy. cancel: no energy. Gathering and travel cost extra.
abilities.effects: Examine records colour, heft, firmness by touch, visible damage, whether the interior is exposed, visible deterioration (of the interior only once exposed), your own eating record and your records of that food with their evidence; shape, edibility, safety, toxins and nutrition stay unknown. Strength is hardness/10. A strike passes the lower of the implement and support strength times (1 - flexibility); if that is not above the food strength the food holds: the trial fails and the work ends. Otherwise each strike adds damage (load - strength)/strength, kept on the unit; at 1 the outer layer splits open, else it stays cracked and closed. Soft food opens by hand at once. The unit stays one carried unit with its mass, eating profile, origin, age and decay; part masses are not represented, so nothing detaches. Opening is not tasting, cooking or detoxifying and certifies nothing; eat uses the existing rules. Opened units cannot be planted. An unworked round pauses; cancel or death releases the unit once as it is (at death, on the ground). No refund, repair, reward or wellbeing. Records are unverified.

The specification is self-consistent and the existing ecology grounds propagation, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Reuse: ex16 already developed cultivate-plants@1 for the same request, and the ex17 specification fits it with small differences. long-plant-cultivation.ts now builds both packages from one factory, cultivation(variant). The ex16 variant keeps its id, scope long-ex16, handler long.cultivate-plants, 1.5-energy rounds, modes plant/tend/inspect/end, texts and events. Its serialized package is byte-identical to before; ex16 replay compatibility, ex7-ex15 replay compatibility and the three ex16 test files are unchanged and pass. The ex17 variant is a new package, plant-cultivation@1, in scope long-ex17, with handler long.plant-cultivation and equivalence cultivation:plant-propagule:trial-inspect-tend:1 (learning 3; the ability serializes to 3,473 code units, within the 3,500 limit). Its package id differs because package keys and handler ids must be unique across the registry. Further reuse: ex15 cultivation-trial@1's law constants, treated-unit list, ageing, plant, observation-input, footprint and reach helpers through its existing exports; its cultivation-trial drawing (visualComponents ['cultivation-trial']); the unchanged open-ecology.ts establishment, growth, dispersal and spacing law; forest-environment.ts ageing; long-planting-site.ts; collective-work.ts escrow, paid work and stop; open-foundation.ts probe and personal records; and base gather. Implemented (ex17). Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant of the same food. x, y name a 0.25 m plot within reach on hand-workable ground, under the existing long-planting-site rule: ordinary meadow soil '.', no water or wet bank, waterlogging at most 0.1, clear of people and reserved objects. The site also needs local soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and fewer than 3 plants of that food or prepared plots within 5 m. Every check runs before any cost, so a refusal spends nothing and gives the observed reason. Round 1 (1 energy) escrows the unit, still carried, owned and ageing, and creates the plot (cultivation-site-prepared). Round 2 (1 energy) rechecks reach, site, unit and energy, then moves the unit with its origin, mass and age into the plot as an unowned reserved stack that cannot be eaten or used, and records its decay at transfer. The plot gets exactly the seedling data that the dispersal law gives a natural propagule (cultivation-propagule-planted; no food is created; no qualified flag, so no practice milestone). It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture, waterlogging and season. At the existing threshold (12; 60 for woody plants) the unit is absorbed into the new plant (cultivation-plot-established). Stock then grows one unit per growth interval up to min(4, source capacity) (cultivation-crop-matured at the first unit) and is harvested only through unchanged gather. If the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies and stops growing (cultivation-trial-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge (cultivation-work-paused). Plant resumes the person's own work and pays only the remaining round (cultivation-work-resumed). Production ledger: from placement, the hidden plot data (not in public fields or event metadata) records accounted rounds, qualifying rounds with positive growth, establishment, post-establishment growth, units produced and units removed by gather, foraging or dispersal; stock always equals produced minus removed, and a dead plot accounts no further rounds. Inspect (one round, 0.2 energy): with inputStackId, it checks one owned unreserved unit and reports resource, quantity, origin, harvest tick, decay, condition (1 - decay/lifetime), represented treatments, buds 'not represented', viability 'unknown', and whether it can be planted with the exact refusal reason. With x, y as well, it applies the exact plant site check at a site within reach and reports ground, moisture, waterlogging, regime and the reason. Nothing is consumed or reserved; this is an unverified personal record (cultivation-condition-observed, scope unit). With target, a plant source or plot in reach is observed through the baseline probe, as in ex16. Inspect-progress (target a plot in reach; one round, 0.2 energy through the baseline probe) compares lifecycle, stage, visible stock and sprouted with the same person's previous plot record, or with the covered state at placement. It returns 'changed' with each field's before and after, or 'inconclusive', and reports the window (20 rounds, endsAt, open, nextCheck among 5, 10, 20) as an unverified record (cultivation-condition-observed, scope plot). Tend (target a planted or sprouted plot in reach; any learner; one round, 0.5 energy) records the same visible-state observation and checks the 0.6 m clearance for competing plants (cultivation-plot-tended, with competingPlants and removed 0); it adds no water, nutrient or growth, and a tended plot establishes exactly like an untended control. Abandon (one round, no energy) acts only on the person's own unfinished planting and returns the unit once in its current condition. It clears the empty site (cultivation-trial-ended); after placement it is refused at no cost, and the plot and unit stay. Death before placement stops the work and leaves the unit, unowned, where the person died (cultivation-trial-failed); a placed unit stays planted. Nothing is refunded. Differences from the specification and modeling assumptions. (1) The species and material recipe is the existing general plant law, not a meadow-root botany model. Viable input: a whole untreated unspoiled unit from a living plant of the same food. Environmental ranges: planting moisture 0.3-1.2, and growth driven by temperature (root minimum 3, optimum 16), light, soil and climate moisture, waterlogging and season. Rooting: establishment 12 accumulated growth, so its duration depends on conditions and no fixed date is promised. Survival and decay: the buried unit keeps its food ageing (root lifetime 240), and spoiling kills the plot. Harvestable mass: stock units times resource mass (root 0.4). Retained living structure: the plant object itself, which gather never removes, so complete destructive harvest is not an available operation and renewal continues. Regeneration interval: the source plant's interval. Carrying capacity: min(4, source capacity). The same law applies to every food with a growth cycle and an ageing lifetime. (2) Water and nutrients exist in that law only as rate factors (soil moisture, climate moisture, waterlogging, depletion), not as stocks a plant consumes. The ledger therefore records production and losses but debits no pool, because adding a pool only for planted plots would make them grow differently from natural seedlings under the same law. (3) Quantity is 1 per plant action: each further unit needs its own plot, input and full cost, so the four roots are never spent automatically. (4) Shoots and buds are not represented on harvested units, so inspection says so instead of reporting them. (5) Competing growth: the existing rules start no plant within 0.6 m of another object, and growth does not depend on neighbors, so no competing growth can stand in a plot's clearance. Physical removal is therefore not implemented: a plant found there through some other rule is reported and left in place. (6) Inspections are allowed at any time; the 20-round window and its checks at 5, 10 and 20 are reported as a schedule and change nothing. (7) Unit and site inspection spend the 0.2 observation cost directly rather than calling the probe, because the probe's observe mode on a carried stack records only the person's own soil; plant sources and plots use the probe itself. (8) Retrieving a placed unit is not supported, as the specification allows. (9) The specification's proposed stages map to preparing, planted (no sprout seen), established (sprouted, with harvestable stock in the drawing), dead and ended. 'Stressed' is not a separate stage: stalled growth shows only as unchanged visible state. (10) Death leaves unplaced material on the ground where the person died, because the world has no estate. (11) No satisfaction, pleasure or comfort source is added: the review's optional bounded practice and information benefits are not required by the specification and were left out. Records are unverified, so the existing information-gain rule applies only through the probe's own dated-change rule. (12) Hand work needs no tool and is limited to ordinary soil; forest floor, dry hard ground and wet ground are refused. Soil moisture is read locally at the site, not taken from the reported 0.65. At Wren's current position the ground is forest floor, so planting there is refused at no cost. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex17-plant-cultivation.test.ts) cover scope separation from ex16, unique handlers, the size limit and excluded vocabulary, learning, the two 1-energy rounds, conservation, the hidden ledger, establishment equal to a natural control seedling, absorption, ledger accounting through stock and gather, rot failure and the inconclusive and changed progress looks, cost-free refusals, unit and site inspection without consumption, tending at 0.5 energy without growth change by another learner, a reported but unremoved plant in the clearance, pause, resume and planter-only abandon, another food (berry) and death.

Wren's round-156 request (Practical root cooking: prepare an owned meadow root into a cooked meal with explicit material, heat and energy requirements, no assumed fuel, tools or heat, no guaranteed improvement) received the World Agent decision develop (learning 3): a general thermal food preparation with modes prepare-hearth, ignite, tend, cook, inspect, retrieve, extinguish and cancel, a minimal physically gated hand-friction fire, the smallest dry-roasting process without pot, water or metal tools, one whole root per trial, conservative nutrition, unchanged spoilage and eat path, and no reward. The specification is self-consistent, so this is not a first release: implemented hearth-food-preparation@1 (scope long-ex17, ability hearth-food-preparation, handler long.hearth-food-preparation; renamed from an earlier draft id so that revisions, handlers and exports stay unique beside the separate long-ex18 thermal-food-preparation@1 package). Existing fire representations were searched first: local-fire@1 (forest-fire.ts, a stone hearth, friction kit, combustion and warming of people tied to thermal-refuge satisfaction) is not installed in long-ex17 and stays byte-identical; its values are reused here without its satisfaction trigger, warming or reward. prepare-hearth: two paid rounds of 1 energy clear a 0.45 m bare bed (local-fire footprint) on meadow, dry or forest ground that is not water, a ford, wet or saturated soil, under open sky, 0.7 m clear of objects, loose items and people (local-fire clearance); no stack is created; the hearth object has createdBy null so observers see only its public mode and progress. tend: 1 round, 0.5 energy, moves owned branch, bark or dry grass (the local-fire fuel set, tenths, bed capacity 8 mass) from inventory onto the bed and/or turns the cook's own food. ignite: needs an unlit hearth loaded with at least 0.5 dry grass tinder and 0.5 branch kindling, an owned whole board of soft wood (branch or willow, hardness at most 3) and an owned whole spindle of a harder wood (birch or oak), all at moisture at most 0.35, rain at most 0.15 and wind at most 0.65 (local-fire ignition limits); pieces are reserved, carried and returned worn with a recorded socket and worn mass; up to 12 drilling rounds of 1.5 energy are paid only when performed, then an ember transfer round and a first tending round of 0.5 energy each, burning 0.1 dry grass each; an ember not worked in the next round dies; failure after 12 rounds leaves worn pieces, drill dust as hearth residue and no fire. Combustion reuses local-fire@1 rules as values: at most 1 fuel unit per round times (1 - moisture), per-unit fuel values from the resource table, 10% ash and 90% released gases, embers three rounds after the last burn, rain above 0.6 douses it; loose fuel lying within 0.25 m of a lit bed catches and joins it. cook: 1 round, 0.5 energy, lays exactly one whole owned unspoiled root or berry (foods whose water composition the world represents) on the bed, reserved and owned by nobody, so it cannot be eaten, planted, given or cooked elsewhere; one portion per hearth; on a bed above 60 C placing, turning and retrieving need an owned whole branch as a stick (not consumed); retrieve takes the food by hand only when its surface is at most 50 C and the bed at most 60 C, otherwise the stick rakes it aside to cool in air; extinguish (1 round, 0.5 energy) smothers the fire with the soil cleared from the bed, leaving unburned fuel; inspect (1 round, 0.2 energy) records the perceivable hearth, fuel wetness and food surface condition plus a model estimate of rounds and fuel to the cooked criterion as an unverified personal record, never the core temperature, or checks up to four owned items by touch; cancel (no energy) ends unfinished clearing or drilling and returns reserved pieces once; death drops them where the person died while fire and food continue. Events: hearth-work-progress, hearth-prepared, hearth-work-paused, hearth-work-resumed, hearth-work-cancelled, friction-progress, friction-ember-formed, friction-ember-died, friction-ignition-failed, hearth-ember-transferred, hearth-ignited, hearth-fed, hearth-fuel-burned, hearth-extinguished, hearth-material-caught, hearth-food-placed, hearth-food-turned, hearth-food-changed, hearth-food-raked, hearth-food-retrieved, hearth-inspected; practice evidence is the retrieval event, which never carries a qualified flag, so cooking earns no milestone. The cooked unit keeps its identity, origin, harvest date and decay and keeps ageing under the unchanged rule; its char is scraped off as hearth residue; it eats through the unchanged eat handler as one unit at its original nutrition times its remaining unburnt solids share (never above 14 per root, never more for water loss), through the existing per-stack food-profile hook, which is read only for this record in worlds with this operation installed and gives no new meal method or quality, so no meal-variety or pleasure change; whole units are required because the existing eat path in this world consumes whole units only. Modeling assumptions (declared, not discovered facts): thermal time of one round is 18 minutes (one eightieth of the 80-round day), used only inside the heat integration; 1 local-fire fuel unit releases 2 MJ (a 1.1 kg branch holds 8 units, about 16 MJ of air-dry wood), which overstates light fuels such as dry grass and bark because their existing per-unit fuel values are kept; fuel and wood moisture follows the local-fire rule (current rain when untracked, +0.08*rain per rainy round outdoors, else -0.01*(1+wind)); hand drill 20 W at the contact, dust heat-loss conductance 0.04 W/K raised by half the wind, dryness factor 1 - moisture/0.35, socket warm-up 15 K per consecutive worked round, ember at 350 C with 2 g of dust, socket abrasion 1.5 mm per round with full contact at 3 mm, board wear 1.5 g and spindle wear 0.5 g per round; bed of about 5 kg soil and ash with heat capacity 4 kJ/K and loss 3 W/K to the surroundings (about 600 K above ambient at the full burn rate); food as a 1000 kg/m3 sphere split into two 15% faces and a 70% core, root water fraction 0.75 from the existing food water representation, heat capacity 4.18 kJ/kg/K for water and 1.5 for dry matter, bed contact coefficient 15 W/m2K on the lower face, still air 10 W/m2K, conductivity 0.5 W/m/K over half the radius, evaporation at 100 C with 2.26 MJ/kg, charring of dry tissue above 200 C at 2e-5 per K per second with 30% char yield and 70% gases, no moisture migration, shrinkage or char insulation; labels: cooked when the core has been at least 85 C for a cumulative 10 minutes, charred at 20% of solids burnt, destroyed below 10% remaining solids, with no claim of nutritional improvement, safety, detoxification, sterilization or longer shelf life. Heat and mass are ledgered exactly: released fire heat equals bed storage plus loss to the surroundings plus heat delivered to food, food heat equals its enthalpy change plus losses to air, vapour and pyrolysis gases, and food mass equals remaining water, solids and char plus evaporated water and gases; fuel burned equals ash plus released gases. Not modeled: warming or burning of people (the bed is solid and hot handling is blocked rather than injuring), ignition of vegetation (excluded by the placement clearance), other ignition routes or heat sources (no sun, sparks or spontaneous ignition), vessels, water, racks and multi-portion cooking. Reuse: local-fire@1 values and hearthSpatial, forestFireFuel, the food water composition, collective-work escrow and paid work, open-foundation personal records, unchanged gather, pickup, drop and eat. A new open-hearth drawing shows only actual state (dashed while cleared, fuel, drill during friction, glow only for embers, flame only while burning, smoke only with combustion, food colored by its modeled state). Current ex17 weather note from the frozen climate formula: at round 156 rain is about 0.8 and stays above 0.15 until about round 232, while wind stays below 0.65 until about round 296, so friction ignition is physically gated to that calm, dry window with material gathered after the rain or kept dry; in the tests, dry pieces in a calm warm spell form an ember on the second drilling round and pieces kept at moisture 0.34 fail after 12 rounds.

Sol's round-161 request (Inspect and handle unfamiliar food: assess an owned gathered food unit by feasible examination, report observable condition, established food-use knowledge and uncertainty, and allow simple handling such as opening a shell when physically possible, without guaranteeing safety, removing toxins, creating food or awarding wellbeing) received the World Agent decision develop (learning 1): one general examine-and-mechanically-handle-food operation with an owned inputStackId, quantity of one whole unit, mode examine or open and optional toolIds/supportTargetId; examine at one round and 0.2 energy without material use; open at 0.5 energy per performed round under a physically validated resistance-and-force test; blocked attempts at no cost, paid failed trials, damage kept as progress, a conserved composition ledger, pause/resume/cancel/death semantics and no reward. The specification is self-consistent, so this is not a first release. Registry check first: the long-ex17 registry holds only the baseline interfaces (navigate, rest, wait, pickup, gather, eat, drop, give, message, request, learn, probe, consult, exchange, name, mark, tell, invite), plant-cultivation@1 and hearth-food-preparation@1. None opens a food unit: probe press/wet/heat consumes a 0.1 sample, consult only reads records, plant-cultivation inspects planting units and the hearth only heats roots or berries. The ex10 examine-food@1 and the ex13 hazelnut opening packages are outside this scope (the ex13 ones are bound to single specimens), so they stay unchanged and only their rules are reused as values. Implemented mechanical-food-handling@1 (scope long-ex17, ability mechanical-food-handling, handler long.mechanical-food-handling, export LONG_MECHANICAL_FOOD_HANDLING, file long-mechanical-food-handling.ts, events prefixed food-handling-, registered last in V7_PACKAGES; none of the package ids or file names reserved by other branches is used). examine (1 round, 0.2 energy, nothing used or reserved) writes a personal unverified record and emits food-handling-examination-started and food-handling-examined with: shape 'not represented', color, per-unit mass, firmness by touch, visible damage and crack progress, whether the interior is exposed, visible deterioration from the current decay share (of the interior only once exposed), the person's own eating record (memory.discoveries) when one exists, up to six personal records about that food with their keys, ticks and evidence event ids, and an explicit unknown list (shape, part masses, edibility and nutrition without an eating record, safety, toxins, interior condition while closed). It never reads hidden nutrition or toxicity and shows no edible or safe flag. open (1 round per performed attempt, 0.5 energy paid through workPay) reserves one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit through workReserve (it stays carried, owned and ageing) and performs one attempt per round; cancel (no energy) stops unfinished work. Resistance-and-force test from existing material values: strength = hardness/10 and flexibility/10 from openMaterial. A strike passes the load min(implement, support) of strength x (1 - flexibility). By the probe press law the food holds when its strength is not below that load: the trial is paid, food-handling-trial-failed is emitted, the unit returns unchanged and the work ends. Otherwise each strike adds damage (load - strength)/strength, kept on the unit: below 1 the outer layer is cracked and still closed and the unit stays reserved (food-handling-damaged; the operation continues or pauses); at accumulated damage 1 the outer layer splits open and the interior is exposed (food-handling-opened). Bare hands open only food of hardness at most 1 (the examine-food@1 rule that harder food needs a hard implement), at once in one paid round; hands never crack firmer food. In this world a gathered stone (0.8) on a stone rock opens a hazelnut (0.4) in one strike, an oak piece (0.7 x 0.8 = 0.56) needs three strikes, and a fallen-branch implement or support (0.3 x 0.8 = 0.24) holds. Blocked attempts (food-handling-blocked, no energy, no new job, a paused job stays paused): firm food by hand, a support without an implement, an implement without a support, more than one implement, a food, non-rigid (hardness below 1) or equipment implement, a support that is not a solid, unreserved object of a represented material or not in reach and view, and energy below 0.5. Identity and form errors (unknown, foreign, reserved, non-food, otherwise treated, already opened or fractional units) are refused before any cost. Progress: the job records method, implement, support, attempts and damage; the unit carries processing.foodHandling (parents, workId, outer cracked or split open, interior, damage, attempts, openedAt, openedBy and a ledger). An unworked round pauses without cost (food-handling-paused); open again resumes after rechecking unit, implement, support, reach and energy (food-handling-resumed) and keeps the job's implement and support unless new ones are named; cancel and death (onDeath; the unit is left on the ground where the person died, matching the existing death placement) release the unit once in its current state with no repair or refund (food-handling-cancelled); a unit that spoils while reserved stops the work. Only the owner can resume or cancel. Modeling assumptions: the load-transmission rule (the weakest or most flexible body in the load path limits the load); damage accumulation (load - strength)/strength with opening at 1, and immediate opening of zero-strength food; the hand threshold taken from examine-food@1; food flexibility is not used; one decay value for the whole unit, shown as exterior deterioration and as interior condition only once exposed (examine-food@1 classes below 0.25 and 0.65); the support's material is its data.resource; no tool wear, because under the existing contact law a body at least 0.5 harder takes none and no deformation law exists for a softer implement (the implement and rock are touched, not changed; contacts are counted on the job). Composition ledger: the world represents no shell or interior composition for any food, and the specification forbids inventing a shell mass from the label, so the parts stay together. The opened product is the same single unit (quantity 1, original mass, eating profile, origin, harvest date and decay, ordinary ageing); its ledger lists outer layer and interior with part masses not represented, 0 detached fragments and 0 losses. No extra edible unit, debris or resource is created; separating the interior from the shell into separate items is not implemented in this version. Eating keeps the unchanged eat rule (an opened unit eats exactly like an unopened one). Cracked or opened units carry a processing record, so plant-cultivation refuses them as treated. Experience: records are unverified (no information-confirmed), the practice evidence event carries no qualified flag (no milestone), and there is no satisfaction, wellbeing, comfort or nutrition change. Visuals: visualComponents is empty; events carry view metadata (operation, mode, actor, target and product ids, position, progress, outer and interior state, fragments 0, tool contact, outcome and uncertainty), and a product id appears only after the split commits. Reuse: open-physical.ts openMaterial; open-foundation.ts openRemember; collective-food-profile.ts (read only); forest-food-accounting.ts unit mass; forest-references.ts resolution; collective-work.ts escrow, paid work and stop; continuous-geometry.ts reach and visibility; the examine-food@1 hand rule and classes; the probe press law; and the ex17 plant-cultivation@1 and hearth-food-preparation@1 unit-inspection, paid-work and record patterns. No existing package is changed; hearth-food-preparation@1 and plant-cultivation@1 behavior and text are untouched. The ability serializes to 2932 code units (limit 3500). Tests cover scope, the text limit, vocabulary and one study round; examination cost, cited personal and eating records, the unverified record and no reward; blocked attempts that spend nothing and refused identities; one-strike opening with conservation, an unchanged implement and rock, unchanged ageing and eating, and the planting refusal; three-strike accumulation with pause, resume and the owner-only rule; paid failed trials for a weak implement and a weak support; cancel returning a cracked unit and a later attempt continuing from its damage; hand opening of a soft root splitting one unit off a stack; and death placement.
